item.title: The New Delegation Stack
item.description:
Computers historically automated only tasks with precisely specified procedures.

Large language models introduce a new layer: machines that can receive ambiguous goals, reason about approaches, and delegate work across different levels of intelligence and cost.

Future software architectures may dynamically allocate intelligence the way operating systems allocate compute.

item.title: How Much Can an Interview Actually Measure?
item.description:
Every evaluation system has limited resolution.

An interview, benchmark, or committee can only distinguish capabilities within the range it is designed to measure.

Understanding evaluator capacity is essential for building better selection systems.

item.title: Evals Are the New Engineering Artifacts
item.description:
Traditional software relies on explicit specifications. AI systems increasingly require a different contract: the ability to measure whether behavior is good.

Evaluation becomes a core engineering artifact.

It defines what success means, creates feedback loops, and allows intelligent systems to improve.
